Note::RegexAccessor::match¶

Back to Note API Reference

Signature¶

Note Note::RegexAccessor::match(std::string_view pattern) const

Test Whether A Whole Cell Matches A Pattern¶

match(pattern) reports, for each cell, whether pattern matches the entire cell — anchored at both ends, as if the pattern were wrapped in ^(?:...)$. It is the validation predicate of the regex family: use it to check that a field has exactly the shape you require (a well-formed date, a key, a code) before trusting it.

Because the match is whole-cell, a pattern like \d+ passes only for a cell that is nothing but digits; to accept “contains a digit run somewhere”, either loosen the pattern (.*\d+.*) or use search.

pattern is an ECMAScript regular expression. An invalid pattern throws pluss::Error before any cell is tested.

Return value¶

A Bool Note with the receiver’s shape, one native truth value per cell. Use bools() for a borrowed contiguous host view.

Example 1: Anchored — The Whole Cell Must Match¶

const auto n = pluss::make_note({"2026", "year 2026", "none"});
const auto mask = n.regex().match(R"(\d+)");
std::cout << "[";
for (std::size_t i = 0; i < mask.bools().size(); ++i)
  std::cout << (i ? ", " : "") << static_cast<int>(mask.bools()[i]);
std::cout << "]\n";

Output¶

[1, 0, 0]

Only "2026" is entirely digits; "year 2026" has other characters.

Example 2: Loosen The Pattern To Accept Extra Text¶

const auto n = pluss::make_note({"2026", "year 2026", "none"});
const auto mask = n.regex().match(R"(.*\d+.*)");
std::cout << "[";
for (std::size_t i = 0; i < mask.bools().size(); ++i)
  std::cout << (i ? ", " : "") << static_cast<int>(mask.bools()[i]);
std::cout << "]\n";

Output¶

[1, 1, 0]

Example 3: An Invalid Pattern Is Rejected¶

try {
  pluss::make_note({"x"}).regex().match("(");
} catch (const pluss::Error& e) {
  const std::string msg(e.what());
  std::cout << msg.substr(0, msg.find('\n')) << "\n";
}

Output¶

regex().match: The expression contained mismatched ( and ).

See Also¶

  • Note::RegexAccessor::search: the unanchored version; it matches anywhere in the cell.

  • Note::RegexAccessor::findall / Note::RegexAccessor::replace: extract or rewrite matches.

  • Note::is_digit and the is_* family: fixed character-class checks with no regex engine.
